title: World War Two
examples: What were the main groups fighting in World War Two?
Can you tell me about a major turning point in the war?
How did the war start in 1939?

explain.say: The war started in 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.
The main groups fighting were the Allies and the Axis powers.
A major turning point was the Battle of Britain in the summer of 1940.
Another key turning point was the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941.
The war finally ended in 1945 with the surrender of Japan.
In everyday life, understanding alliances helps us today.

items: Countries form treaties for mutual support.
These agreements are like historical alliances.

faq.q: When exactly did World War Two end?
faq.a: The war officially ended in 1945 after the surrender of Japan.
asks: When did the fighting finally stop?

faq.q: Who were the main sides fighting in the war?
faq.a: The main sides were the Allies, which included the USA and Britain, and the Axis powers.
asks: What were the two main groups?
Can you name the opposing sides?

faq.q: What is a turning point in a war?
faq.a: A turning point is a moment where the tide of the war changed direction greatly.
asks: Can you give an example of a turning point?

faq.q: Why did the war start in 1939?
faq.a: The war started in 1939 due to Germany's invasion of Poland.
asks: What event kicked off the war?
What was the start date of the conflict?

faq.q: Were all the countries in the Allies always together?
faq.a: No, the alliances changed over time as the war progressed.
asks: Did the groups stay the same?
Were the alliances stable throughout the war?

facts: The war began in 1939 with the invasion of Poland.
The Allies included major powers like the United States and Great Britain.
The Axis powers included Germany, Italy, and Japan.
The Battle of Britain was a critical turning point in 1940.

quiz.say: The war started when which country invaded Poland?
quiz.why: Germany's invasion of Poland marked the beginning of the war.

wrong.0: Italy was a major Axis power, but not the initiating force.
wrong.1: Britain was a key member of the Allies, not the invader.
wrong.2: The USA entered the war later, after Pearl Harbor.

quiz.say: Which event is considered a major turning point in the war?
quiz.show: Battle of Britain or Pearl Harbor?

options.show: Both the Battle of Britain and Pearl Harbor were major turning points.
options.say: Both the Battle of Britain and Pearl Harbor were major turning points.

quiz.why: These events significantly shifted the balance of power during the war.

wrong.0: This was the start of the war, not a turning point.
wrong.1: This was the end of the war, not a turning point.
wrong.2: This describes the groups, not a specific moment of change.

quiz.say: The war concluded in which year?
quiz.why: The surrender of Japan in 1945 marked the end of the fighting.

wrong.0: This year saw major events like Pearl Harbor, but not the end.
wrong.1: The end date is a specific historical year, not a calculation.
wrong.3: This is when the war began, not when it ended.
